chapter: Childhood in Tyler, Beaumont and Houston
title: Olin's decline and a plot for revenge
summary: After the murder the theatre failed and Olin went downhill; in 1930 Gus and Olin planned to get the killer until Olin's mother stopped them.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: So what about Olin?
And the theater didn't last long after that. She tried to run the theatre.
That was the idea, I guess, huh? Put it out of business.
Put him out of business, because he was doing too much for the black man in Houston at the time.
He was the head of the NAACP.
He was the president of the NAACP there.
My gosh. What happened to Olin?
Well, after that, it was downhill for him.
I should think it might be, too. I can quite see how it would be.
Well, --
I mean, that's terrible, isn't it?

Yes. You see, they opened a barbeque place there. They did very well with that. And I came down to visit them. In 1930, I visited them. And they had the barbeque place. Truthfully, we intended to get even with this guy.
Yeah, I should think so.
We really did.
I should think I could quite believe you, for his father.
And his mother got wind of it, and she put the boots to us. She stopped that.
What, in about 1930, you mean?
Yes.
When you came back?
Yes. Oh, we had it all planned. We were going to get him for it.
I should think --
And she happened to hear us plotting.
And you kids would have only been about 17 or 18 then? Or a little older? In '30, let's see --
'30, no, I was about 16.
And you kids were going to do that?
[Yes, I was, yes, I was.]
What, were you going to beat him?
We didn't care. We were going to get him. And we would have.
He had the nerve to be around, go around?
Oh, yes, well, he was paid so much and they caught him and put him in jail. But he got out. He got out.
They got him paroled.
Sure, that's right. He didn't stay in no time.
What a terrible thing. Everybody knew, I guess.
Sure, they knew, they knew. They knew exactly.
He was certainly lucky, wasn't he, not to have --
That's right. He's dead now, though.
What a terrible thing. It's bad enough to happen, anyway, let alone a man like that be bought.
That's right. So that messed up things for Olin, so --
And put him on the wrong track, huh?
Right. And he just turned out the
other way.
He was bitter.
Yes, it just upset him altogether. I don't even know what happened to him after that, whether he's living or dead.
What a horrible thing. That's a terrible shame.
